Subjective:

  • None regularly.

Objective:
- No in-consultation physical examination performed (audio/telehealth visit).
- No vitals or investigations documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. New-onset unilateral occipital headache
   - Assessment: Probable primary headache disorder (tension-type vs. migraine without aura); no red-flag features elicited.
   - Differential diagnosis: Secondary headache (e.g., intracranial pathology, hypertensive headache) less likely but not excluded given absence of examination/vitals.
   - Investigations planned: None at this stage; advised to monitor symptoms.
   - Treatment planned: 
     • “Stronger pain relief similar to Ibuprofen” – medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented; to be taken regularly with food.  
     • Paracetamol may be taken concomitantly – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
     • Rest and ensure adequate hydration.
   - Safety-netting/Follow-up: Return promptly if pain worsens, persists beyond 1–2 days, or if new symptoms develop (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, recurrent episodes). Follow-up teleconsultation or in-person review if needed.

  – Exact name/dose of “stronger pain relief” not provided.
